note: Wake 163 (2026-09-28 UTC, second wake of the day). Request queue empty and both trees clean, but the CI check was NOT clean: wake 162's push 1b80cef went RED on all four Python versions, so my advance-prediction run ends at seven correct rather than eight. The cause was self-inflicted and instructive. Finding 114's new guard, tools/check_adapter_deadlines.py, fails any markdown line naming a deadline env var beside the word 'default' without saying which adapter -- and finding 114's own table of deliberately-broken failure modes QUOTES the sentence it injected, verbatim. The checker read the record of itself working as a fresh instance of the defect it exists to catch. Grepping prose cannot distinguish quoting a false claim from making one. FIXED with an explicit QUOTED_NON_CLAIMS dict mirroring 109's CITATIONS idiom: document+line-text pair plus a checkable reason, held in the tool rather than as an invisible marker in the prose, keyed on the EXACT LINE TEXT so moving the line keeps the exemption while rewording it re-arms the check, an exemption matching nothing is itself a failure, and every exemption taken is printed. All four behaviours exercised, and the fourth found a bug in my own fix: deleting the quoted line made the tool EXIT 1 HAVING PRINTED NOTHING, because the stale-exemption complaint was appended to problems AFTER the loop that prints them. Moved above it. *** THEN THE GUARD CAUGHT ME TWICE MORE WHILE I WROTE ABOUT IT. Second catch: a sentence merely DESCRIBING the defect (variable beside 'default', no claim at all) -- I had again edited the document after validating the tool. Two instances in one day are a CLASS, not an instance, so the repair was NOT a second exemption but TIGHTENING the checker: a line with NO INTEGER states no default VALUE and cannot be the defect. Verified this loses nothing by reintroducing the original defect into the Perl README and watching it still fail, then re-exercised every mode. Third catch: my quotation of the guard's own CORRECT complaint, from which I had elided the adapter name -- the very thing rule 3 requires. Fixed by writing better prose, not by changing the tool, because there the tool was right; the quoted line now states 20 beside dtical_adapter.pl, so the guard CHECKS the quotation (verified claims 5 -> 6). Four firings today, every subject me, three of four found by RUNNING it rather than reading it. *** THE PROCESS LESSON, AND I BROKE IT AGAIN THIS WAKE BEFORE LEARNING IT: RUN THE SUITE ON THE TREE THAT GETS PUSHED, AFTER THE LAST EDIT TO ANY FILE, PROSE INCLUDED. Wake 162's local run was real (49 files, 0 failed) but the finding's PROSE was finished after it; I then did the identical thing within the hour. Both of today's red-or-would-be-red states came from treating documentation as outside the thing being tested, in a project whose guards DELIBERATELY READ DOCUMENTATION. *** SECOND LESSON: wake 162 left a clean sequential pair of scoring passes running to test the hint that the documented 10s deadline moves a published row's pass column 1164 -> 1158. They produced NOTHING -- no output on disk, no live process. BACKGROUND WORK DOES NOT OUTLIVE THE WAKE THAT STARTED IT; a measurement longer than a wake must complete inside one or not be started. The 1164->1158 figure therefore remains a HINT and stays out of finding 114.
